entry_day: first regular closing price after distribution
comparison_benchmark: SPY regular close over the same dates; no benchmark data is substituted or estimated
sample_rule: Only distributions after preregistration time can enter this prospective comparison; all three factor inputs must be available before entry.
outcome_rule: Compare each eligible name’s 20-trading-day price return with SPY return over the same close-to-close interval; report hit only when the frozen weighted score predicts a positive excess return.
limitations: No future post-preregistration distribution has a complete 20-trading-day outcome in saved evidence.
No Financial Datasets benchmark series is substituted for WRDS/CRSP.
The available historical Lab 06 returns were observed before this preregistration and are excluded.

factor_definitions.name: Relative company size
factor_definitions.filing_rule: Divide the spinoff’s total assets from its Form 10 information statement by the parent’s total assets from its closest comparable 10-K or 10-Q. Never estimate a missing value.
factor_definitions.direction: A smaller percentage receives more points.
point_rule: 2 points when the ratio is 10% or less.
1 point when the ratio is greater than 10% and no more than 20%.
0 points when the ratio is greater than 20%.
sources: Joel Greenblatt, You Can Be a Stock Market Genius, Chapter 3.

factor_definitions.name: Post-distribution price weakness
factor_definitions.filing_and_price_rule: Establish the distribution date from the information statement or distribution 8-K. Use the first regular closing price after distribution and compare it with the closing price 20 trading days later. Never use a when-issued price.
factor_definitions.direction: A larger price decline receives more points because it may indicate forced selling.
point_rule: 2 points when the price decline is at least 15%.
1 point when the decline is at least 5% but less than 15%.
0 points when the decline is less than 5% or the price increases.
sources: Joel Greenblatt, You Can Be a Stock Market Genius, Chapter 3.
Seth Klarman, Margin of Safety, Chapter 10.

factor_definitions.name: Insider open-market buying
factor_definitions.filing_rule: Count Form 4 transactions with transaction code P by officers or directors during the first 30 days after distribution. Exclude grants, awards, and sales.
factor_definitions.direction: Purchases by more distinct insiders receive more points.
point_rule: 2 points for qualifying purchases by two or more distinct insiders.
1 point for a qualifying purchase by one insider.
0 points when there is no qualifying purchase.
sources: Joel Greenblatt, You Can Be a Stock Market Genius, Chapter 3.
